raw_response:
I have been farming this same land for most of my life. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil, I know this weather, and I know what works. My 12 mu does wheat in winter and maize in summer — same land, same rotation I have done for decades. The well is reliable, so I am not worried about dry spells.

**For wheat:** I plant in October after the maize comes off. I buy improved seed from the village cooperative — the Jimai variety has treated me well for years, no need to change. I do rotary tillage to break up the maize stubble. I put down base fertilizer before planting — urea and some diammonium phosphate mixed together — then top-dress with urea around jointing. Potash I use a little, not much, I never saw a big difference from more. Irrigation three times: once before the ground freezes in November, once at jointing in April, once at heading in May. My son helps me with the sprayer — two passes, one for weeds early, one for powdery mildew before heading. I expect around 420 jin per mu on a normal year.

**For maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct seed hybrid maize — Zhengdan 958, everyone uses it, the yields are good. No tillage, the ground is already soft. Base fertilizer goes in at planting, then I side-dress nitrogen at the 8-leaf stage when the plants are knee-high. I water twice — once if it is a dry June, once around tasseling if there is no rain. One pesticide pass for corn borer, usually in late July. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

My household of four people can handle this themselves with some help at harvest. Nothing fancy, but steady.
